name: Awesome AI Resources (The Definitive AI Resources Repository)

categories.title: AI Governance Resources
categories.intro: Global research institutes, policy bodies, and government AI safety institutes shaping frontier governance.

items.title: Centre for the Governance of AI (GovAI)
items.desc: Advancing research on the governance and societal impact of artificial intelligence.

items.title: Leverhulme Centre for the Future of Intelligence (LCFI)
items.desc: Interdisciplinary research on the implications of artificial intelligence for humanity.

items.title: Cambridge Centre for the Study of Existential Risk (CSER)
items.desc: Researching global catastrophic risks, including those posed by advanced AI, to safeguard humanity’s future.

items.title: Cambridge Centre for AI in Medicine (CCAIM)
items.desc: Focusing on AI applications in healthcare and medical research.

items.title: Center for Human-Compatible AI (CHAI)
items.desc: Pioneering research on aligning artificial intelligence with human values and interests.

items.title: Future of Life Institute (FLI)
items.desc: Multidisciplinary research centre exploring existential risks and transformative technologies.

items.title: Future of Humanity Institute (FHI)
items.desc: Archive – https://www.futureofhumanityinstitute.org/ Closed by the University of Oxford in April 2024 after 19 years. The archive preserves its substantial research contributions on AI risk, existential risk, and longtermism. Research in these fields continues at GovAI and other successor organisations.

items.title: Mimir Center for Long-Term Futures Research
items.desc: Independent research institute advancing long-term futures and AI risk scholarship, founded with researchers from the former Future of Humanity Institute.

items.title: Oxford Internet Institute
items.desc: Exploring the societal implications of the internet and digital technologies.

items.title: AI Now Institute
items.desc: Comprehensive research on the social implications of artificial intelligence.

items.title: Institute for Law and AI
items.desc: Examining the intersection of artificial intelligence and legal systems.

items.title: Ada Lovelace Institute
items.desc: UK-based independent research institute examining the social and ethical implications of AI and data, with strong policy impact.

items.title: Alan Turing Institute
items.desc: The UK’s national institute for data science and artificial intelligence, fostering research across academia, government, and industry.

items.title: Stanford Human-Centered AI Institute (HAI)
items.desc: World-leading interdisciplinary research on human-centred AI, spanning technical, ethical, social, and policy dimensions.

items.title: MIT Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory (CSAIL)
items.desc: MIT’s flagship AI and computer science research laboratory, producing foundational AI breakthroughs.

items.title: Georgetown Center for Security and Emerging Technology (CSET)
items.desc: Research on the security dimensions of emerging technologies, with particular focus on AI and geopolitics.

items.title: Tony Blair Institute for Global Change
items.desc: AI – https://institute.global/ Policy-focused analysis on AI’s global governance and economic impact, aimed at governments and policymakers.

items.title: Data & Society Research Institute
items.desc: Independent research addressing the social and cultural issues arising from data-centric technological development.

items.title: AI Index (Stanford HAI)
items.desc: Annual report tracking AI progress across research, education, economics, ethics, and policy — the definitive reference for AI trends data.

items.title: Institute for AI Policy and Strategy (IAPS)
items.desc: Exploring and guiding the transformative potential of advanced AI through rigorous policy research.

items.title: Partnership on AI
items.desc: Multistakeholder organisation developing best practices for responsible AI development and deployment.

items.title: AI Policy Exchange
items.desc: Global platform for AI policy research and dialogue across governments, academia, and civil society.

items.title: EU AI Office
items.desc: The European Commission’s central body for implementing the EU AI Act and overseeing general-purpose AI models.

items.title: UNIDIR
items.desc: Disarmament and AI – https://unidir.org/ The United Nations Institute for Disarmament Research, conducting landmark research on AI in security contexts including autonomous weapons systems.

items.title: Simon Institute for Longterm Governance
items.desc: Supports international policy processes on transformative technologies.

items.title: Campaign to Stop Killer Robots
items.desc: The leading international coalition of civil society organisations advocating for a preemptive ban on fully autonomous weapons. Publisher of the LAWS Disarmament Toolkit.

items.title: European AI Pact (EU AI Office)
items.desc: European Commission initiative driving early voluntary industry commitments ahead of full EU AI Act obligations (succeeding the former AI Watch monitoring portal).

items.title: UK AI Security Institute (AISI)
items.desc: The world’s first government-backed AI safety institute, established at Bletchley Park in November 2023 and renamed AISI in February 2025. Tests frontier models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, and Meta. Publishes the open-source Inspect evaluation framework. Has tested over 30 of the world’s most advanced models.

items.title: NIST AI Risk Management Framework
items.desc: The US National Institute of Standards and Technology’s comprehensive AI RMF — the global benchmark for AI risk management, adopted by governments and enterprises worldwide.

items.title: EU AI Act (Full Text)
items.desc: The world’s first comprehensive, binding AI regulation, adopted in 2024. Sets risk-based requirements for all AI systems deployed in the EU and affecting EU citizens.

items.title: Japan AISI
items.desc: Japan’s AI Safety Institute, established in February 2024. Conducts frontier model evaluations and participates in the international AISI network.

items.title: Bletchley Declaration
items.desc: The landmark 2023 international declaration on AI safety signed by 28 countries including the US, China, and UK — a milestone in global AI governance.

items.title: RAND Center on AI, Security, and Technology (RAND CAST)
items.desc: Policy analysis and technical security research hub within RAND covering AI x Bio, frontier model security controls, and geopolitics.

items.title: Frontier Model Forum
items.desc: Industry body founded by leading frontier AI labs focused on advancing technical safety evaluations, threat sharing, and responsible model deployment.

items.title: NIST CAISSI (US AI Safety & Standards Institute)
items.desc: NIST’s Center for Advancing Innovation and Standards for Super Intelligence (formerly US AISI / CAISI), leading US federal AI evaluations, standards, and testing guidance.

items.title: International AI Safety Report
items.desc: Landmark international scientific synthesis chaired by Turing Award laureate Yoshua Bengio and backed by 30+ nations, surveying capabilities, systemic risks, and mitigations.

items.title: UN High-Level Advisory Body on AI
items.desc: United Nations multistakeholder advisory body advancing recommendations for global AI governance capacity building and international coordination.

items.title: Lawfare — Artificial Intelligence
items.desc: In-depth legal and national-security analysis examining AI regulation, export controls, autonomous systems, and constitutional doctrine.

items.title: Centre for Long-Term Resilience (CLTR)
items.desc: Independent UK think tank advising governments on extreme risks from frontier AI, biosecurity, and national resilience planning.

categories.title: AI Safety Resources
categories.intro: Technical alignment labs, capability evaluators, and binding international safety standards.

items.title: Alignment Research Center (ARC)
items.desc: Dedicated to ensuring advanced AI systems are aligned with human interests, including evaluating dangerous capabilities in frontier models prior to deployment.

items.title: Machine Intelligence Research Institute (MIRI)
items.desc: Pioneering research on ensuring beneficial artificial intelligence through mathematical and decision-theoretic approaches.

items.title: EleutherAI
items.desc: Open-source AI research collective focusing on large language models, mechanistic interpretability, and AI safety. Creator of the Pile dataset and GPT-NeoX.

items.title: Center for AI Safety (CAIS)
items.desc: Promotes research on reducing societal-scale risks from advanced AI. Behind the widely-cited 2023 AI risk statement signed by leading AI researchers.

items.title: Anthropic Research
items.desc: Anthropic has a leading AI safety team. Its research covers constitutional AI, mechanistic interpretability, alignment science, and responsible scaling. Publishes extensively in peer-reviewed venues.

items.title: Redwood Research
items.desc: Safety-focused AI lab working on adversarial robustness, interpretability, and dangerous capability evaluations.

items.title: Apollo Research
items.desc: Independent AI safety organisation specialising in evaluating deceptive and dangerous capabilities in frontier AI models.

items.title: METR (Model Evaluation and Threat Research)
items.desc: Conducts rigorous autonomous capability evaluations of frontier AI models. Works directly with leading labs ahead of model deployment.

items.title: Cooperative AI Foundation
items.desc: Advances research on making AI systems cooperate effectively with humans and with each other.

items.title: OECD AI Principles
items.desc: Guiding ethical, human-centred, and accountable AI development globally. The most widely-endorsed international AI principles framework.

items.title: EU Artificial Intelligence Act
items.desc: The world’s first comprehensive binding AI regulation. Required reading for anyone operating in AI governance, law, or policy.

items.title: NIST AI Risk Management Framework
items.desc: The US government’s authoritative framework for managing AI risks. Widely adopted globally as a governance and compliance standard.

items.title: ISO/IEC 42001:2023
items.desc: The international standard for AI management systems — the AI equivalent of ISO 27001. Covers governance, risk management, and responsible AI practices across the full lifecycle.

items.title: ISO/IEC 23894:2023
items.desc: Guidance on organisational risk management for AI systems development and deployment.

items.title: Model Card Frameworks
items.desc: Tools promoting transparency by documenting AI models’ use cases, limitations, and performance metrics.

items.title: Singapore Model AI Governance Framework
items.desc: A framework offering detailed guidance on ethical and governance issues for AI in the private sector. Highly practical and internationally influential.

items.title: Anthropic Responsible Scaling Policy
items.desc: Anthropic’s published commitments on when to pause AI development based on dangerous capability thresholds. A model for the field.

items.title: AISI Inspect Evaluation Framework
items.desc: The UK government’s open-source AI safety evaluation toolkit, freely available to researchers, companies, and governments worldwide.

items.title: MIT AI Risk Repository
items.desc: Living database from MIT FutureTech cataloguing 1,000+ AI risks across causal and domain taxonomies for policymakers, researchers, and risk teams.

items.title: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI
items.desc: The first global standard-setting instrument on AI ethics, adopted by all 193 UNESCO member states. Covers human dignity, rights, sustainability, and inclusion across the full AI lifecycle.

items.title: Council of Europe Framework Convention on AI
items.desc: The first binding international treaty on AI, signed by Council of Europe member states and key partners including the US, UK, and EU. Establishes a human rights framework for AI development and deployment.

items.title: Transformer Circuits Thread (Anthropic)
items.desc: Open mechanistic interpretability research series dissecting internal features, circuits, and sparse autoencoders inside large language models.

items.title: SecureDNA
items.desc: Cryptographically privacy-preserving global DNA synthesis screening system safeguarding biosecurity alongside frontier AI biological capability safeguards.

items.title: MATS (ML Alignment & Theory Scholars)
items.desc: Flagship research mentorship seminar pairing independent safety scholars with senior mentors from leading alignment labs.

items.title: FAR.AI
items.desc: Non-profit AI safety research lab conducting foundational work in adversarial robustness, mechanistic interpretability, and alignment evaluations.

items.title: Palisade Research
items.desc: Independent technical research group investigating offensive cyber capabilities, emergent behaviour, and loss-of-control risk in frontier models.

items.title: Google DeepMind Responsibility & Safety
items.desc: Google DeepMind’s Frontier Safety Framework, dangerous capability evaluations, and bio/cyber safeguard research.

items.title: OWASP Top 10 for LLM & GenAI Applications
items.desc: Industry-standard open security checklist detailing prompt injection, excessive agency, sensitive data leakage, and AI supply-chain risks.

items.title: MITRE ATLAS
items.desc: Adversarial Threat Landscape for Artificial-Intelligence Systems: living knowledge base of real-world attacks and mitigations against AI systems.

items.title: Higgsfield
items.desc: A full creative workspace that aggregates 15+ leading AI video models — including Seedance 2.0, Kling 3.0, Veo 3.1, Wan, and others — under one subscription, allowing you to switch between models and compare outputs without leaving the platform. Its flagship feature is Cinema Studio, which simulates real optical physics — letting you choose a virtual camera body, lens type, and focal length before generating — and can lock characters across shots and stack multiple camera movements to create footage that looks and feels shot on a real film. Free tier available; paid plans from $9/month.

items.title: Hailuo AI (MiniMax)
items.desc: The best argument in 2026 that free AI video doesn’t mean low quality. Its daily credit refresh lets you generate multiple clips per day at no cost — and quality for realistic human video, including facial expressions, lip sync, and emotional range, is substantially above what its zero price point would suggest. Built by MiniMax, a Chinese AI company, and excels at generating videos of people — face expressions, lip sync, and portrait-style footage. If your use case involves human subjects, Hailuo consistently outperforms competitors on the free tier. Free tier (daily credits); paid from ~$9.99/month.

items.title: Luma Dream Machine (Luma AI)
items.desc: Ray3 is the first AI video model with native 16-bit HDR output, aimed at professional colour pipelines. It handles fluid dynamics, cloth simulation, and rigid-body collisions well enough to consistently fool human evaluators in blind tests. Known for realistic physics — one of the most important things in AI video generation, as it makes videos feel weighty and lifelike — with fast generation times typically around 15 seconds.
